inline_comments.comment: `FreeElectrons` is imported from `ase.calculators.test`. The `.test` module path reads like a test fixture rather than a legitimate model, which may confuse readers encountering this gallery example. A brief inline comment such as `# Simple analytical free-electron model` would clarify that this is an intentional, usable calculator and not a stub used only for unit tests.

`emin=0` means the plot starts exactly at the Fermi level, hiding all of the occupied band structure below it. The `BandStructurePlot.plot()` signature documents `emin` as "minimum energy *above* reference" and defaults to `-10`. For a gallery example meant to illustrate what a band structure looks like, starting from a negative value (e.g. `emin=-10`) would show the occupied and unoccupied bands together, making the example more informative. This value was inherited from `doc/ase/dft/bs.py`, but the migration is a good opportunity to revisit it.

general_comments.comment:
The migration is incomplete. The PR only adds `examples/gallery/bs.py` but does not remove `doc/ase/dft/bs.py` or update `doc/ase/dft/kpoints.rst`, which still contains:

```rst
.. literalinclude:: bs.py
.. image:: cu.png
```

Leaving both files in place means the old example continues to exist in a separate doc location, and both scripts will generate `cu.png` independently during the build. The `kpoints.rst` page also needs to be updated — either by pointing its code snippet and image to the sphinx-gallery output, or by replacing the `literalinclude`/`image` directives with a cross-reference to the new gallery entry.

The module docstring contains only the RST title and no explanatory prose. While `examples/gallery/ptable.py` follows the same title-only pattern, a one- or two-sentence description of what the example demonstrates (e.g., what `FreeElectrons` models, what the k-point path covers, what the output plot shows) would make the gallery entry more self-contained and useful to readers browsing the rendered gallery.
